subject: Recap + Proposed POC: OrionX evaluation sprint, success criteria & owners
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@orionx.ai>, Anna Ruiz <anna.ruiz@orionx.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + Proposed POC: OrionX evaluation sprint, success criteria & owners

Hi Liam / Anna —

Thanks again for the demo earlier today. Quick recap and a proposed next-step POC plan so we can align expectations and owners before we lock dates. I pulled together an evaluation outline (attached) and a short SLA draft for review.

Recap (brief):
- Goal: Reduce query latency for priority inference paths and validate model quality on OrionX production samples (~50k tokens/day).
- Primary success metrics you called out: 95th-percentile latency <= 250ms (end-to-end), model output F1 on intent extraction >= 0.92, and throughput to handle peak batch windows (~200 concurrent requests).
- Constraints: On-prem deployment for PHI-scrubbed logs (we discussed private deployment + KMS), IDP procurement window in mid-April.

Proposed POC (3-week lightweight sprint):
1) Week 0 (prep, 3 business days): access exchange, test data sample (sanitized), baseline telemetry capture. Owners: OrionX data (Anna), Redwood infra (Karthik).
2) Week 1 (integration): private agent setup in your VPC, model pinning, basic routing rules, and smoke tests. Owners: Karthik (Redwood) / Anna (OrionX).
3) Week 2 (load + quality): run synthetic and production-sample load, collect latency distributions, run eval prompts, and compare outputs against baseline. Owners: Marissa (Redwood CS) / OrionX data lead.
4) Week 3 (wrap & decision): run final acceptance tests, review cost/throughput tradeoffs, and a decision meeting to move to Reserved capacity.

Acceptance / Success criteria (proposed):
- Latency: 95th <= 250ms for representative production flows (measured over a 30-minute 95th window).
- Quality: intent extraction F1 >= 0.92 on held-out sample; no regression > 2% on main model prompts.
- Reliability: zero major infra-induced 500s during 24-hour soak test.
- Operational: observability (traces + token-level cost) and runbook for failover in place.

Logistics / blockers we flagged:
- Need sanitized sample (50-100 conversations) and an SSH jump host + KMS access for the private agent staging environment.
- Procurement: expect legal review on the SLA draft (attached) — timeline may push to late April unless procurement accelerates.

Ask / next steps (proposed):
- Anna: confirm who will provide the sanitized test sample and whether org can provision a staging subnet for the private agent by Mar 12.
- Liam: confirm the success criteria above or suggest edits by EOD Wed (Mar 7).
- Redwood: we’ll schedule a 45-minute technical kickoff once we have staging access — propose Tue Mar 14 or Wed Mar 15 (we can work to your timezone).

I've attached a short POC evaluation outline and a draft SLA for review. Happy to adjust scope if you want a narrower acceptance criteria set or longer soak window.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: redwood_poc-eval-outline.pdf (5 pages), redwood_trial-sla-draft.docx
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@orionx.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anna Ruiz <anna.ruiz@orionx.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Mar 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + Proposed POC: OrionX evaluation sprint, success criteria & owners

Thanks Soojin — solid recap. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Samples: Anna will provide a sanitized set of ~80 conversations by Tue (Mar 7) morning. Confirmed.
2) Latency target: 95th <= 250ms is aggressive but worth testing; can we also capture 99th so we understand tail behavior?
3) Throughput: the 200 concurrent requests estimate is correct for our busiest window. We also want to measure cold-starts for cache misses.
4) Security: procurement will want to see the KMS flow end-to-end and a list of logs collected (we will share an internal compliance contact).

Edits to acceptance: add a 99th percentile latency capture and add a one-week observational period post-POC to validate stability.

We can do the kickoff on Wed Mar 15 (we're on PDT). Legal will review the SLA but likely needs edits around data retention and audit logs.

I’ll mark Mar 7 for the sample and Mar 15 for the kickoff.

—Liam
Head of Platform, OrionX
liam.oconnor@orionx.ai
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@orionx.ai>, Anna Ruiz <anna.ruiz@orionx.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 06 Mar 2028 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + Proposed POC: OrionX evaluation sprint, success criteria & owners

Great — thanks for the quick turnaround Liam. Noted: we will capture 99th percentile latency and include a one-week observational window after the main tests. Revised acceptance criteria below.

Revised acceptance (summary):
- 95th <= 250ms; 99th capture for tail analysis (no hard pass/fail, but documented).
- Intent F1 >= 0.92, regression gate <= 2%.
- Zero infra-induced 500s across the 24-hour soak; plus stability checks during 1-week observation.

Logistics follow-up: Anna — can you drop the sanitized sample link and a contact for your procurement/compliance reviewer by Tue EOD? If you confirm staging subnet by Mar 12 we’ll lock the kickoff for Mar 15.

Marissa / Karthik: can you confirm internal owners and quick checklist items we need to run the private agent in their staging environment? I put a short checklist in the attached outline but will paste the two critical items here:
- SSH jump host (IP and SSH key) + service account with minimal permissions.
- KMS key ARN or service account and short description of key rotation policy.

Thanks — I’ll update the Drive doc once Anna shares the sample.

Soojin
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@orionx.ai>, Anna Ruiz <anna.ruiz@orionx.ai>
Date: Wed, 07 Mar 2028 10:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + Proposed POC: OrionX evaluation sprint, success criteria & owners

Quick tech note / commitments from Redwood infra: 
- I’ll own the private agent bootstrap and staging orchestration (tile the agent to your subnet, set kernel/quantization profile appropriate for your GPU type).
- Need: staging subnet CIDR, a bastion host (we prefer ephemeral key via Jump), and the sanitized sample.
- We’ll instrument the 95th/99th latency buckets and publish a short dashboard link (read-only) during the trial. Expect the first baseline telemetry within 48 hours after staging is live.

Operational constraints to flag: if your staging GPUs are <16GB, we’ll recommend a quantized runtime and may need to adjust batch sizes — this will affect observed latency/cost tradeoffs. We should surface that in the kickoff so procurement understands the potential performance delta.

I’ll prepare a short runbook for the Mar 15 kickoff and link the dashboard to the Drive doc.

—Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
